findings.title: Lowering maxPayout to cap an already-large uncapped pot is front-runnable: a mempool-watching NFT holder burns first and takes the full pot, so a retroactive cap never binds
findings.description: maxPayout defaults to 0 (unlimited) and pause does not stop accrual. The natural owner reaction to a pot that has grown large (long idle stretch, or a multi-day pause) is setMaxPayout(cap), which _checkpoint()s and would forfeit the excess. But burn() is permissionless and reads the pot at its own execution time, so any NFT holder who sees the owner's setMaxPayout in the public mempool can burn in the same block ahead of it and receive the entire uncapped pot (minted as antimatter, which is unpausable and has no supply cap). The cap only ever binds if it was set BEFORE accrual exceeded it. Pausing first does not help: the pause() tx is equally front-runnable and pause only blocks future burns. A competent owner reading the story ('maxPayout ... prevents a long idle period from turning into one large mint'; 'Admin setters stay callable while paused') could reasonably believe a cap applied after the fact protects the pot - it does not. Same mechanism applies to the first burn after unpause() (back-run of the unpause tx collects everything accrued during the pause).
findings.attackVector: 1) setRatePerDay(2.5e18) with maxPayout==0; 100 days pass (or contract is paused for a long incident). Pot = 250e18. 2) Owner broadcasts setMaxPayout(10e18). 3) Searcher holding any claim NFT (all tokenIds equal; cheapest-index NFT suffices) sees it and submits burn(id, 0) with higher priority in the same block. 4) Searcher receives 250e18 antimatter; owner's cap tx lands afterwards on an empty pot. PoC: work/test/audit23/BonfireCapFrontRun.t.sol (test_CODE001_frontRunBurn_defeatsCap PASS: payout 250e18; control test_CODE001_capLandsFirst_payoutCapped PASS: payout 10e18).

findings.impact: Bounded by ratePerDay x elapsed time: an over-mint of antimatter (convertible to phUSD via Antimatter.annihilate) relative to the owner's intended cap. No user principal at risk; issuance-policy leak. Quantification of antimatter value is econ-scanner's lane.
findings.recommendation: Operational (no code change needed): set a non-zero maxPayout BEFORE or in the same tx/bundle as the first non-zero setRatePerDay, and treat it as a standing cap, never a reactive one; send any later cap reduction via a private relay. Optional code hardening: have setRatePerDay revert when enabling a rate while maxPayout==0, or make pause() also checkpoint-and-freeze accrual.
findings.dedupHint: Same root as LOCAL-001/PATTERN-002 (default-unlimited cap + accrual through pause). Merge into that finding as its 'retroactive cap is unenforceable' facet unless dedup prefers a separate call-sequence entry. Not in ledger (no NFTBonfire entries exist).

findings.title: Cross-project premise expiry: NFTBonfire gives every NFTMinterV2 claim NFT a permissionless holder-callable redemption (pot of antimatter), invalidating the 'NFT has no realizable redemption value' basis of phoenix-nft-staking wont-fix 858e9e80 and the conditional-harm reasoning on 521c20ad
findings.severity: informational (re-weigh trigger; possible Low/Medium in phoenix-nft-staking after econ quantification)
findings.description: Before story-053 the only burn paths on NFTMinterV2 were authorised-burner contracts (SYA claim). phoenix-nft-staking run-21 closed the BatchNFTMinter nudge-gate finding 858e9e80 as wont-fix on the explicit verified premise that 'NFTMinterV2 has no holder-callable redeem/claim/withdraw path', so the freshly-minted NFTs a nudge snatcher receives are sunk cost. NFTBonfire, once wired (setAuthorizedBurner + Antimatter.setApprovedMinter + non-zero rate), is exactly such a path: any holder of any tokenId can convert 1 NFT into the current pot. Every authorised NFTMinterV2.mintFor caller (e.g. the NFTMigrator granted setAuthorizedMinter in phStaging deploy scripts) and every cheap mint route therefore now mints a redeemable ticket. The realisable value per NFT is bounded by the winner-takes-all pot per accrual interval (the Nth NFT in one interval is worth ~0), so this does NOT by itself prove the nudge gate is now profitable - it moves the bound from 0 to ~ratePerDay x inter-burn interval (capped by maxPayout). The run-21 closure rationale must be re-evaluated against that number; per the expired-closure rule this is its own bucket, not a regression.
findings.attackVector: Conditional: BatchNFTMinter(MultiToken) nudge pot P is claimed by a searcher who receives nudgeSize NFTs; previously value 0, now at least one of them can be bonfired for the pot whenever pot > 0. If P + bonfirePot > qualifying cost, the run-21 '~6.7x sunk-cost margin' argument no longer holds. Also: mintFor-authorised contracts become antimatter faucets bounded only by the pot rate.

evidence.code: RESOLVED: the NFT has NO realizable redemption value ... ledger 858e9e80 flipped fixed -> wont-fix

findings.recommendation: Route to phoenix-nft-staking: re-weigh 858e9e80 (gate) and 521c20ad (race) with bonfire pot economics once phStaging sets the live ratePerDay/maxPayout; record the bonfire rate/cap as a live re-arm trigger. Owner should audit the NFTMinterV2 authorizedMinters set (revoke stale NFTMigrator-type grants) before enabling the bonfire rate.
